text: Fluvanna Events Roundup: weekly civic newsletter that warms local owners up for the $750 Watchdog Intake Engine.

rec.title: Fluvanna Events Roundup + consulting funnel

make.why: A standalone civic name keeps the roundup separate from your studio and consulting brands.
The locked sequence, from hero through Featured, Weekend, daily listings, filters, Spotlight, Coming Up and submit, built once and refilled every Thursday.
Front: free Spotlight invite. Back: Featured slot rates. It's your opener with Alliance contacts.
One reusable weekly graphic, since Facebook is only for distribution links.
The Google Form, Sheet tab, RoundupEngine.gs and Gemini prompt are Workspace work, so build them in your Gemini or Claude Code chat.

deliver.why: Beehiiv builds issues in its own editor, so the design is the master copy and any other sender can use the file as is.
Easy to email or leave behind after a Spotlight interview.
Sizes for a Facebook link preview and a feed post.

build.starter: Design project: HTML email for the issue, Flier for the one-pager, a fixed-size component for the share card
order: Lock the name, then the masthead
Issue template filled with one real week (15 to 20 events + 1 Spotlight)
Share card, last, taken from the issue's look
build.count: 1 email template (8 sections), 1 two-sided one-pager, 1 share card in 2 sizes

top.name: Organic
top.why: Warm and neighborly, which suits Lake Monticello families, events and local services.

backup.name: Classical
backup.why: A weekly-paper feel that sponsors take seriously, though stiffer for festivals and kids' events.

look.custom: Leave Industry for the consulting practice. Email clients often drop Caprasimo, so set a safe fallback headline font in the issue.

scope: Issue template with the first real issue
full.turnaround: 3 to 5 days once the name, the Featured price and the first week's events are in

setup.why: Organic doesn't exist as a system yet. Build it first, then attach it to a Design project for the three pieces.
steps: Create the Organic design system, using the roundup's name as its brand
Open a Design project and attach Organic
Gather 15 to 20 verified events for one real week
Gather one Spotlight business (e.g. Reliable Rides): blurb, photo, link
Set the Featured slot price and what it includes
Paste the first prompt, then invoke HTML email
setup.firstPrompt: Build the weekly issue template for [Name], a free Thursday 7 AM events email for Fluvanna County and Lake Monticello (Palmyra, Troy, Fork Union, Zion Crossroads). Use HTML email, single column, mobile first. Sections in this order: hero with free-weekly promise; Calendar at a Glance with daily counts and a verified-on stamp; Featured This Week (paid slot); This Weekend, then Mon to Wed daily listings; intent filters (Today, This Weekend, Free, Live Music, Family, Business/Networking); Local Business Spotlight with a 'Want your business featured?' button; Coming Up; and a submit-your-event close linking to [form URL]. Each event is one line: emoji, title, time at linked venue, one sentence, and a Free or Registration required tag. Footer credit to House Pomare. Fill it with the attached real events and spotlight.

gaps: Which name: The Fluvanna Loop, Lake & County Weekly, or another?
Featured slot price, and what does a sponsor get (logo, link, length)?
Is Beehiiv final, and does your plan allow custom HTML blocks?
Do you have one real week of events and a first Spotlight ready?
Do you want the weekly share card, or links only?
rec.next: Pick the name and Featured price, send the first week's events, and say go.

text: Client workbook, formatted to print and look good.

rec.title: Client printable workbook

make.why: The full workbook: cover, contents, sections, exercises and writing space.
A fixed set of page types (section opener, lesson, exercise with lines/boxes, checklist, reflection) so every page looks consistent and she can add more later.
Only if buyers will type into it on screen instead of printing.

deliver.why: Prints cleanly at home or at a print shop, and is easy to sell or email.
Lets you edit copy and add pages later without rebuilding.

build.starter: Design project with the paged-document starter, one explicit page per sheet so writing space and exercises land exactly where intended
order: Get her content as a doc: sections, exercises, prompts
Design 4 to 5 page types plus the cover
Pour in the content section by section
Proof a test print, check margins and line spacing for handwriting
build.count: About 20 to 40 pages, depending on her content (cover + contents + 4 to 5 page types repeated)

top.name: Their own brand
top.why: A workbook she sells or hands to clients should match her logo, colors and fonts.

backup.name: Organic
backup.why: Warm, friendly and print-friendly, which suits coaches, wellness and personal-growth workbooks.

look.custom: Keep print in mind: light pages, ink-friendly color, generous writing lines, 11 to 12pt body text.

scope: Full workbook with all her content
One revision round after a test print
full.turnaround: 4 to 7 days once content is final

setup.why: A printable document, not slides. Build the look as a Design System first if she has a brand and it's not set up yet.
steps: Get her full workbook content in one doc (Google Doc, Word or plain text)
Collect her logo, colors, fonts and any photos
Confirm page size (Letter or A4) and whether it's home-printed or print-shop
If she has a brand: create her Design System first, then attach it
Start a Design project and paste the first prompt
setup.firstPrompt: Build a printable workbook for my client using the paged-document starter, [Letter/A4], one page per sheet. Topic: [topic]. Audience: [who]. Make a cover, a contents page, and these page types: section opener, lesson page, exercise page with writing lines and boxes, checklist, reflection page. Use generous writing space and 11 to 12pt body text. Her content is attached. Lay out section 1 first so I can approve the look.

gaps: What's the workbook about, and who uses it?
Is her content written already, or does it need writing?
Roughly how many pages or sections?
Will it be printed at home or at a print shop, and does she want it fillable on screen too?
Does she have a logo, colors and fonts?
rec.next: Answer the gaps, or send her content and say go.

text: Client shirt: one design on the front, one on the back.

rec.title: Client shirt: front and back

make.why: The main graphic, sized to the printer's front print area.
The second graphic, sized to the back print area.
Both sides on a shirt photo so the client approves before anything prints.

deliver.format: Print PDF, one page per side
deliver.why: Type and shapes stay sharp, and most printers accept PDF.
Backup for DTG/DTF printers that ask for raster files.
Easy to text or email the client for sign-off.

build.starter: Design project, canvas mode: two artboards at print size plus a mockup sheet with image slots
order: Get the printer's specs: method, ink colors, print area, file type
2 to 3 front/back concept pairs side by side
Client picks one, then one round of revisions
Mockup sheet on their shirt color

top.name: Their own brand
top.why: Merch should carry the client's logo, colors and fonts.

backup.name: Custom shirt direction
backup.why: If there's no brand: set it per shirt (mood, 1 to 3 ink colors, one display font), not a full system.

look.custom: No UI system needed. Shirt art lives on its own: bold type, limited inks, contrast that works on the shirt color.

scope: Mockup sheet on the chosen shirt color
Print PDF + transparent PNG per side
full.turnaround: 2 to 4 days, plus printer proof time

setup.why: Artwork and mockups, not slides. No design system unless the client has a brand.
steps: Ask the printer for specs: print method, max ink colors, print area size, file format
Collect the client's logo, colors, fonts, and any art or photos to use
Get the shirt color and a blank shirt photo (front and back) for the mockup
Gather the exact copy for each side
Start a Design project and paste the first prompt
setup.firstPrompt: Design a two-sided shirt for my client. Front: [copy/idea]. Back: [copy/idea]. Shirt color: [color]. Printing: [screen print, N ink colors / DTG], print area [WxH in]. Show 2 to 3 front/back concept pairs side by side on a canvas, each side as an artboard at print size. Then add a mockup sheet with image slots for blank shirt photos. Brand files are attached.

gaps: What's the shirt for: event, business merch, team, band?
Do they have a logo or brand files, or art to use?
How is it printed: screen print (how many ink colors) or DTG/DTF? Who's the printer?
Type-led, or illustration? Illustration needs supplied art or an artist.
rec.next: Answer the gaps, or say go.

text: Universal AI Calibration and Audit Skill: an on-call audit skill for Claude.ai chats and projects. Checks Claude's work for gaps, finds a better flow, learns rules from critique. Personal use first, sell later.

rec.title: AI Calibration and Audit Skill

make.why: Runs only when you say "check your work". Stress test, better flow, then one rule learned.
Tone, punctuation and formatting apply to every reply, so they belong in instructions, not the skill.
Where learned rules are kept. A skill can't save its own memory.

deliver.why: A folder with a SKILL.md, uploaded once and available in every chat and project.
The baseline rules: profile for every chat, project instructions for one project.
The log. You paste each learned rule in, and every chat in the project reads it.

build.starter: No design starter. Write it in chat.
order: Split the text into baseline rules and the audit loop
Write SKILL.md: trigger phrases, audit steps, output shape
Audit output: Gaps found, Better flow, Rule learned (one line to paste into the log)
Drop "acknowledge and confirm readiness", and add a fallback when web search is off

top.name: None needed
top.why: Text only. Pick a look when you build the sales kit.

backup.name: Industry (later)
backup.why: Blueprint grid suits an audit method, for the sales one-pager.

scope: Test script: 3 audit runs to try it on
full.turnaround: About 2 hours, then a few weeks of real use

setup.homepage: None: this is built in Claude.ai
setup.why: Not a Claude Design project. Come back to Design when you package it to sell.
steps: Claude.ai: Settings → Capabilities, then upload the skill zip
Paste the baseline rules into profile preferences, or into a project's instructions
Create a project and add calibration-log.md to its knowledge
Test: ask for work, then say "check your work"
After each audit, paste the Rule learned line into the log
setup.firstPrompt: Here is my calibration and audit skill. Turn it into a Claude.ai custom skill: a SKILL.md that runs only when I say "check your work" or "audit this". Split out the always-on baseline rules as a separate block for my instructions. Each audit ends with Gaps found, Better flow and one Rule learned line I can paste into my calibration log.

gaps: Selling the skill file itself, or selling audits as a service?
Any trigger phrases besides "check your work" and "audit this"?
rec.next: Say go, and the skill, rules block and log get written here in chat.

answered.q: Is this for your own use, or something you'll sell or give to clients?
answered.a: For me to try long enough to sell.

answered.q: Where will it run: Claude Design, Claude.ai projects, or other AI tools too?
Should the Redesign Pitch run on every task, or only on design and structure tasks?
answered.a: Only when I call for it, to check the work for anything missing or a better flow.

answered.q: Do you want the card at all, or only the skill?
answered.a: Not sure what the card does. I want it as a skill.

changes: Audit runs only on call ("check your work"), not on every reply
Baseline rules moved to always-on instructions, separate from the skill
Built and installed in Claude.ai, not Claude Design
Card dropped for now. It returns as a sales one-pager when you sell
